newsitem.title: UK: UK March oil/gas revenue lowest for six months - Bank.
newsitem.headline: UK March oil/gas revenue lowest for six months - Bank.

text.p: British oil and gas revenue in March fell to its lowest level in six months as mild weather hit gas output and international crude prices slumped, the Royal Bank of Scotland said.
Combined oil and gas revenues in March slipped to 47.8 million pounds a day, down 11.9 percent from 54.2 million a day in February, the lowest receipts since September, the Bank said.
Oil revenues fell 3.2 million pounds a day to 30.8 million, the poorest returns since June of last year as both prices and production fell.

March oil output registered 2.58 million barrels a day (bpd) down 57,000 bpd from 2.64 million in February. A short-term gas compression problem at BP's Harding oilfield cost some 40,000 bpd in March.
Average monthly benchmark Brent crude fell to $19.17 a barrel from $20.91 in February but the fall in sterling revenues was restrained a little by a slight weakening in the dollar exchange rate.
Gas revenues slumped 16 percent to just under 17 million pounds a day with production, suppressed by mild weather, off 1.83 million cubic feet a day at 9.393 million.
Total combined oil and gas output was 4.233 million barrels of oil a day equivalent (boe) from 4.613 million boe in February and 4.456 million in March of last year.
